name: Network Information API
plain: Estimated connection type, speed and latency, plus a data-saver flag.
meaning: Lets a site pick light pages on slow links. effectiveType buckets: slow-2g, 2g, 3g, 4g. downlink rounds to 25 kbps steps (capped near 10 Mbps), rtt to 25 ms steps. Type (wifi or cellular) is Android only.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: type
fields.range: bluetooth, cellular, ethernet, wifi, wimax, none, other, unknown

limits.headline: Can see roughly how fast your connection is and whether you turned on data saving
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads and while you stay on it
can: See a rough speed class such as 2G, 3G or 4G
See rounded speed and delay figures
See if data saver is on
Tell Wi-Fi from cellular on Android only
cannot: See your exact speed, since figures are rounded to coarse steps
Tell Wi-Fi from cellular on a computer
See your provider, name or location
limits.differs: Only Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet offer it. Wi-Fi versus cellular is shown on Android only.

story.what_it_is: A page can read your estimated connection type, speed and delay, and if data saver is on.

marketing.name: Network Information API
marketing.pitch: Lets pages adapt to the connection, such as sending less data on slow links or when data saver is on.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt. Sites may load lighter pictures or skip auto video if your line is slow or you turned on data saver. You just see a faster page.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to cut load time, save mobile data and keep users from leaving. It is also quietly counted in some fingerprints. Firefox and Safari do not offer it.

use_cases.example: A video site starts at 480p on a weak connection and moves up when speed improves.
A browser game checks speed before loading its big level pack and offers a smaller pack on slow lines.
A store shows tiny image placeholders first for shoppers with data saver on.
A news site holds back auto play video on slow connections and metered data plans.
A web editor such as Google Docs delays syncing big attachments until the connection is better.
A speed dashboard shows how page load changes by connection type across real visitors.
An ad script reads type, speed and delay as part of a device fingerprint.

technical_bounds: Estimate from recent traffic, not a speed test
Cannot read Wi-Fi name or signal

linkedin.how: Connection type, downlink, RTT collected. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).

history.change: Not supported on desktop; Android support removed
